title: LiteSpec Project Language Record
description: The closed vocabulary a project's prose is checked against: one Term entry per concept, with its meaning, labels per language, rejected synonyms, broader and narrower terms, and closed-set values, plus the mannered terms no page may use.

schemaVersion.$comment: Each release pins one exact shape. A consumer adopting a later release absorbs every difference at that moment, so no minor-compatible range exists between two releases. See litespec/rule/core-authoring.publish-each-release-as-a-complete-contract and litespec/rule/core-authoring.exclude-cross-release-compatibility-work.

terms.description: One entry per concept. Each entry is a Term record; the glossary page renders from these entries.

mannered.description: Terms that substitute metaphor or flourish for direct statement. Rejected everywhere, with no scope.

term.description: The one word or phrase this project uses for the concept.

meaning.description: What the term means, in at most 25 words.

labels.description: The term in each interface language beside English.

rejected.description: Words that name the same concept and must not appear inside the scope.

broader.description: The wider Term this one sits under, where the vocabulary implies one.

narrower.description: The Terms that sit under this one, where the vocabulary implies them.

values.description: The closed set of codes this Term holds, where it names one.

reason.description: Why the synonym is rejected here. Appears in the diagnostic, so a reader fixes the sentence rather than searching for the rule.

scope.description: A regular expression over the documentation-root-relative path, with forward slashes. Absent means every page. A word correct in one module and wrong in another carries the scope of the module that rejects it.

except.description: Compounds in which a rejected word names a different concept, so a match inside one is not reported. Each is matched whole and case-insensitively, the way a term is.

code.description: The stable code the closed set uses.

label.description: The words a reader sees for the code.

instead.description: The literal phrase that carries the same meaning. Appears in the diagnostic as the replacement to reach for.
